A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PDU research, and all supplied text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. v1 ends with references despite mentioning supplementary material; v2 includes Appendices A–B and a checklist. The comparison concerns material actually present in these PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original comparative experiments on TOFU and MUSE-News in Tables 1–2, plus qualitative MUSE-Books responses in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains those benchmark experiments and reports additional Books results, TOFU split results, longer-training experiments, membership-inference evaluations, and jailbreak tests.

M1.justification: The constrained objective, cross-entropy retention loss, squared logit-margin forgetting loss, and warm-started primal-dual updates remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical apart from whitespace. Appendix hyperparameters and expanded explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The data domains remain TOFU and MUSE News/Books; v1 already includes Books examples and names the Forget01/05 splits. v2 adds membership-inference and ground-truth-hinted, single-turn jailbreak scenarios on TOFU in Appendix B.6, extending security testing within the existing domains.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: GradDiff, DPO, NPO, SimNPO, and RMU on TOFU; GradDiff, NPO, SimNPO, and RMU on MUSE, alongside target and retrained models. The added attack procedures are evaluation tools, not new competing unlearning methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds aggregate-success and radar-area metrics, Forget Quality and memorization/privacy evaluations, extended training comparisons at 20/30 epochs and 50 epochs for Forget01, and an adversarial-prompt protocol with modified judge instructions. These substantially extend evaluation design; newly disclosed settings for existing experiments do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 adds training-duration analyses, six membership-inference attacks, exact memorization, extraction strength, privacy leakage, and single-turn jailbreak tests. These examine stability and residual information beyond v1's benchmark comparisons. Tables 6–8 also add detailed TOFU cases, while v1's MUSE response illustration is removed.

E5.justification: Table 15 newly reports Forget Quality hypothesis-test p-values, explained in Remark B.1. Neither version provides repeated-run counts or run-level uncertainty; v2 explicitly acknowledges lacking statistical-significance reporting. Table 16 adds three-number judge-score entries without defining their components, preventing a reliable interpretation as uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All original numerical entries in Table 1 and the MUSE-News comparison are retained. v2 adds Books scores, aggregate scores, Forget01/05 results, and extensive duration and attack results. For example, Table 2 newly reports Books 7B PDU retain/forget ROUGE of 0.413/0.001. These are additional results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies a proof of the existing Proposition 3.1, deriving the maximum-softmax-probability bound through convexity and a Taylor expansion. The proposition itself, constrained formulation, and stated duality assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions and benchmark-performance claims remain. v2 adds an explicit claim of no additional computational or gradient overhead and emphasizes overcoming scalarization's restricted Pareto coverage. These strengthen particular advantages without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of failure under overly tight or loose retention thresholds and their model/data dependence. Appendices B.4–B.6 discuss limitations of Forget Quality, interpreting responses containing supplied jailbreak hints, and model-specific membership-inference vulnerabilities. These considerably extend v1's discussion of tuning, fluency, and untested robustness.

D1.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 and Tables 4–5 disclose hardware, checkpoint sources, optimizer, precision, learning rate, training schedules, and PDU hyperparameters. v2 identifies the judge model and generation settings, provides prompts, and states that PDU is publicly implemented in OpenUnlearning. These substantially fill v1's documentation gaps, although its explicit baseline lambda=1 statement disappears.

R1.justification: v2 adds classical Pareto and epsilon-constrained optimization references, including Bowman, Das and Dennis, and Miettinen, plus memorization and membership-inference literature. The introduction uses these to refine its positioning around trade-off coverage and computational cost. The existing unlearning taxonomy and most prior-method discussion remain.

P1.justification: The introduction's motivation is rewritten, contributions become bullets, and results, limitations, and appendix navigation expand. Structured appendices and a checklist are added. The main section sequence and most existing methodological prose remain; the expansion primarily documents additional technical material rather than extensively rewriting the existing paper.

P2.justification: v2 combines the retained scatter plot with a new method schematic, replacing v1's Books response illustration. It adds radar charts, judge and attack prompt displays, and numerous implementation, example, and analysis tables. Tables 1–2 gain aggregate-score columns, and Table 2 adds Books blocks, substantially expanding the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility and empirical scrutiny: it supplies a missing proof, implementation and judge specifications, and tests of training duration, privacy leakage, and adversarial extraction that expose concrete limitations. These address important gaps in the supplied v1. Reporting flaws remain, including the incorrect harmonic-mean formula in B.4, unexplained Table 16 score triples, and a conclusion still saying jailbreaks were not studied. Nevertheless, the gains in inspectability and supporting evidence clearly outweigh these weaknesses.
